=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py:217-225,357-366 | severity=major | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `--max-time` is applied per curl invocation (per redirect hop) rather than across the whole fetch, so total time can reach about 12 minutes at the default 5 redirects.
  WHY: The documented bound is 120 s total. Severity disagreement: sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT, and the others rated it MAJOR (highest used).
- agents.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md:9 and changelog.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md:10 | severity=nit | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The docs describe "120 s in total" / "120 s total", but the helper enforces the limit per request or hop.
  WHY: Readers will assume a hard 120 s ceiling. Same root cause as the per-hop `--max-time` finding.
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py:222-247 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: MAX_HEADER_BYTES is enforced only after curl returns, so the dump-header temp file is unbounded while curl writes it.
  WHY: A hostile server can consume /tmp disk with headers. Severity disagreement: gemini, minimax and gpt-6-luna rated it MAJOR, glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT, and sonnet-5_5 dropped the claim (it reported NONE and judged it not a real exposure). Highest severity used.
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py:219-251,305-306 | severity=major | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: `--max-filesize` does not cap chunked responses without Content-Length, so the body is only checked for size after the download finishes.
  WHY: A hostile server can exhaust disk before the post-hoc check runs. Severity disagreement: gemini rated it MAJOR, and minimax and glm-5_3-flash rated it NIT. sonnet-5_5 considered it and did not report it.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py:156-205 | severity=nit | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: Only the first validated address is pinned with `--resolve`, so curl cannot fall back to other validated addresses.
  WHY: A dual-stack host whose first address is unreachable causes the fetch to fail. This is also raised as a hardening suggestion by sonnet-5_5, gemini-3_1-flash-lite and glm-5_3-flash.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

(No task gaps reported.)

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (`fetch_url` redirect loop and `_run_single_hop`) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `--max-time` is applied per redirect hop, and nothing tracks total time.
  WHY: Total time can reach about 12 minutes against the documented 120 s.
- agents.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md ("Defaults" bullet), changelog.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md ("Default limits" row) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The docs say "120 s total", but the limit is enforced per request.
  WHY: Same root cause as above. The suggested fix is to reword the docs to "120 s per request" and leave the helper unchanged.
- (Hardening) workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (`_resolve_argument`, `resolve_target`) | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: Only the first validated address is pinned.
  WHY: This causes a failed fetch, not a safety problem. The fix would change both repos together, as a follow-up.
- Dropped by this reviewer (no finding reported): MAX_HEADER_BYTES enforced only after download, and `--max-filesize` on chunked responses.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py:222-225, 243-247 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: MAX_HEADER_BYTES is enforced only after curl returns.
  WHY: An attacker can stream headers and consume /tmp disk.
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py:227-230, 248-251 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Chunked streaming responses are not capped during download.
  WHY: A hostile server can fill /tmp before the post-download size check.
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py:217-220, 361-366 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `--max-time` applies per redirect hop, not to the whole fetch.
  WHY: A fetch can significantly exceed the documented 120 s total limit.
- agents.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md:9, changelog.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md:10 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The docs state a 120 s total limit, which contradicts the per-hop implementation.
  WHY: Operators are misinformed about the operational bounds.
- (Hardening) .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (resolve_target / _resolve_argument) | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: Only the first resolved address is pinned.
  WHY: curl cannot fall back to other healthy addresses. Suggested fix: pin all validated addresses (about 6 lines).
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (`_read_redirect_location()` at line 243-246; `--dump-header` at line 222-223) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: MAX_HEADER_BYTES (1 MiB) is enforced only after curl returns, so the header file is unbounded during the transfer.
  WHY: A hostile endpoint can write many MB of headers into /tmp.
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (`build_curl_command()` at line 218-219; `fetch_url()` loop at line 357-380) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `--max-time` is per hop; the worst case is 720 s at default redirects, and 2520 s at MAX_ALLOWED_REDIRECTS=20.
  WHY: The changelog, agents.md fragment and docstring say "120 s total".
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (`build_curl_command()` at line 220-221; `_run_single_hop()` at line 305-306) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `--max-filesize` is a no-op for chunked responses, and the post-hoc check runs only after the download.
  WHY: A hostile endpoint can exhaust /tmp on small runners.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (and .claude/ copy) (`resolve_target()` at line 156-184; `_resolve_argument()` at line 184-193) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `--resolve` pins exactly one IP.
  WHY: If the first address is unreachable, the fetch fails instead of trying the other validated addresses.
- agents.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md:9 (and changelog.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md:10) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The docs say "120 s total", but the limit is enforced per hop.
  WHY: Agents may be misled about the enforced time bound.
- (Hardening) 3 items: multi-address pinning (`resolve_target()` line 184-189, `_resolve_argument()` line 191-198; risk 1), header-size streaming abort (`_read_redirect_location()` line 243-249; risk 3), per-hop time accounting (`fetch_url()` loop line 357-380; risk 3).
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (`build_curl_command()` lines 222-225; `_read_redirect_location()` lines 243-247; called after curl completes at lines 314-317) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: MAX_HEADER_BYTES is checked only after curl has written the headers to the temp file.
  WHY: Many valid headers can exceed 1 MiB, causing excessive temp disk use.
- .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (`build_curl_command()` lines 218-219; `fetch_url()` lines 357-366) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: `--max-time` is applied per curl invocation, and curl runs again for each redirect. The docs describe it as a total limit (agents.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md:9; changelog.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md:10).
  WHY: Six sequential requests can take about 12 minutes against the documented 120 s total.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (same bytes as .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py) (`_run_single_hop` ~lines 243-250; `fetch_url` ~lines 361-395) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The 120 s `--max-time` is enforced per curl invocation, with no total-time budget. agents.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md line 9 says "120 s in total" and changelog.d/8330-safe-fetch-command-helper.md line 10 says "120 s total".
  WHY: Five redirects that each stall for 120 s keep a fetch alive about 12 minutes, 6x the documented cap.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (same bytes as .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py) (`MAX_HEADER_BYTES` check in `_read_redirect_location` ~lines 222-228) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The 1 MiB header cap is evaluated only after the transfer completes.
  WHY: Disk is consumed temporarily; the header file is cleaned up in `finally`, so impact is temporary disk use, not data loss.
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (same bytes as .claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py) (`build_curl_command` `--max-filesize` ~line 219; post-hoc check in `_run_single_hop` ~line 259) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: `--max-filesize` relies on Content-Length and has no effect on chunked responses, so the byte cap is only checked after the hop finishes.
  WHY: The 100 MiB cap is not enforced during streaming. This is an incomplete mitigation, not a regression, because the raw-curl baseline had no cap.
- (Hardening) workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/safe_fetch_url.py (`_resolve_argument` ~lines 199-205 / `resolve_target` ~line 162) | HARDENING_RISK_SCORE=1
  PROBLEM: Only the first validated DNS address is pinned.
  WHY: A dead A/AAAA record turns a working fetch into a hard failure. Suggested fix: pin all validated addresses as `host:port:addr1,addr2`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
